XV80 Toyota Camry Hybrid Produced in the United States Arrives in Japan After a Three-Year Hiatus
7 photos
Photo: Toyota
The latest Toyota Camry , now only a hybrid sedan in its latest XV80 interpretation, is coming home to Japan - via production units built in the US in Kentucky, as it turns out.
The story of the Toyota Camry nameplate is quite long and extensive – it was first a compact car launched internationally by the Japanese automaker since 1982, and the narrow-body model overlapped for a time with the wide-body version that entered the mid-size market in 1991.
Now it’s one of the best-selling sedans in the world, especially in America, where it found a home-away-from-home – the love affair has been just as long and arduous. The latest iteration came out in late 2023 at the Los Angeles Auto Show in California, and while it retained the same TNGA-K architecture as its predecessor, it has become a hybrid-only model in markets like North America and the Old Continent.
Well, now it’s time for the prodigal son to return home, as Toyota has now announced that the latest Camry, produced at the Kentucky plant in the United States, officially comes back to the Japanese market on December 23, 2026. Just in time to celebrate Christmas a little earlier, right?
Anyway, the Toyota Camry has been absent from its "home" market since 2023, and now it comes as the "Made in the US, Made by Toyota" Camry – as hinted back in June 2026 during the "North American Camry Custom Showdown" event that took place at the Super Taikyu (S-Tai) Fuji 24 Hours, where the Toyota Chairman Akio Toyoda (“affectionately known as Morizo”) explained the ongoing tariff issues might ease off if they sell the US-made Camry in Japan.
The eleventh-generation Toyota Camry thus returns to the Land of the Rising Sun with a US passport, “meticulously adapted for Japanese roads” with right-hand drive, right-sided turn signal switches, and a fully localized Japanese multimedia and navigation system.
Unlike the Toyota Tundra full-size pickup truck and the Toyota Highlander, which are sold in Japan via the bilateral framework agreement allowing the company to skip additional testing for US-certified vehicles, the Camry has been submitted to Japan’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism for official domestic vehicle type certification.
The Toyota Camry is said to be nearly identical in footprint to the Crown Signia crossover, but with a lower roofline, and will be available at home in Japan in two grades: Z and G, starting from ¥5,200,000 or $32,655 for the former and from ¥4,300,000 for the latter, which translates to just $27k at the current exchange rate. In the US, the cheapest 2027 Camry goes from $29,700 sans destination, so the JDM version is actually a sweeter deal for local residents.
Of course, it comes to Japan with the same 2.5L Series Parallel Hybrid System (A25A-FXS) boasting 225 combined horsepower – though it’s only available with front-wheel drive, not also AWD like in America.
